title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_account maintain canonical RLP tuple ordering (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash)?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: SCOPE NOT APPLICABLE - The encode_account function for Ethereum account RLP encoding is NOT implemented in the Prysm codebase. Prysm is an Ethereum consensus layer (beacon chain) client that depends on github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum v1.16.8 for execution layer state management, including RLP encoding of account data. The canonical RLP encoding of account state tuples (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash) is implemented in the go-ethereum library's core/types and rlp packages, which are external dependencies not auditable within the current code scope.

analysis_details.prysm_role: Consensus layer client - does not directly implement execution layer account state encoding
analysis_details.execution_layer_interface: Prysm interfaces with execution clients via Engine API but delegates account state management to go-ethereum types
search_methodology: Searched for RLP-related imports and usage - minimal, delegated to go-ethereum
Searched for Account struct with nonce/balance/storage_root/code_hash fields - not found in Prysm
Verified go.mod dependencies - confirms go-ethereum v1.16.8 dependency
Examined execution layer integration points - uses go-ethereum types
Conclusion: The audit item targets functionality in go-ethereum, not Prysm

potential_issues.description: The audit item CHECK_ID CHK-W5B6-50-001 targets the 'encode_account' function which is part of Ethereum's execution layer account state management. This functionality is implemented in the go-ethereum library (external dependency), not in the Prysm consensus layer codebase being audited.
potential_issues.recommendation: Redirect this audit item to the go-ethereum repository (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum) where the core/types.StateAccount struct and its RLP encoding methods are implemented. Specifically, examine core/types/state_account.go and the RLP encoding in the rlp package.
potential_issues.impact: Cannot perform abstract interpretation on code that does not exist in the current scope

trust_boundary_analysis.data_flow: Prysm (consensus) receives pre-encoded execution payloads from execution clients via Engine API
trust_boundary_analysis.encoding_responsibility: Execution layer client (e.g., geth, which uses go-ethereum library)
trust_boundary_analysis.verification_point: Prysm validates execution payload roots and state roots but does not encode account state itself
trust_boundary_analysis.canonical_encoding_enforcement: Assumed to be correct in execution layer - consensus layer trusts the execution client

recommendations: This audit item should be redirected to audit the go-ethereum codebase where encode_account is actually implemented
If auditing Prysm's interaction with execution layer, focus on: (1) Engine API payload validation, (2) State root verification, (3) Trust assumptions about execution client correctness
For complete coverage, audit go-ethereum's core/types/state_account.go::EncodeRLP() method to verify canonical field ordering
Consider adding integration tests in Prysm to detect non-canonical RLP from execution clients, though this is defense-in-depth rather than primary responsibility
phase1_abstract_interpretation.reason_for_phase_skip: The code under audit (encode_account) is not present in the Prysm codebase. It exists in the external go-ethereum dependency. Abstract interpretation, symbolic execution, and invariant proving cannot be performed on code outside the audit scope. The audit checklist should be updated to reflect the correct codebase target.
